Moisés Evangelista Gamarra\
Servicio Nacional de Adiestramiento en Trabajo Industrial, Perú

The Editor-in-Chief\
*Machine Learning with Applications*\
Elsevier

October 10, 2026

Dear Editor,

We wish to submit an original research paper entitled **"A Reproducible Methodological Framework for Prosecutorial Congestion Risk Prediction Using Explainable Machine Learning and Temporal Validation"** for consideration for publication in *Machine Learning with Applications*.

This paper addresses the problem of anticipating where a public prosecution service is at risk of case congestion. Studies have shown that machine learning can model judicial workload and congestion, but they have focused predominantly on courts, and their evaluations seldom select a model on one period and test it on later ones. It therefore remains unclear how well such models anticipate congestion at the prosecutorial stage when they are applied to future years. Using the open records of the Public Prosecutor's Office of Peru (2019--2026), a leakage-controlled protocol that excludes the variables defining the target, and year-block validation with a hold-out test on 2025 and a prospective evaluation on 2026, we show that the selected LightGBM model reaches an F1-score of 0.469 and a ROC-AUC of 0.798 on the 2025 test set and an F1-score of 0.559 on the 2026 data. An ablation study and SHAP attributions agree that the risk is driven mainly by territorial and institutional configurations rather than by lagged workload. Our findings are significant because they show that open administrative data can support the preventive prioritization of operational combinations, and they delimit that use: the scores can rank combinations for review but are not calibrated probabilities.

Since our study shows how established machine learning methods can be validated over time and interpreted to address a practical problem of public administration, we believe it is a good fit for *Machine Learning with Applications*, which asks application papers to demonstrate how machine learning solves important practical problems. We feel that its findings will be relevant to your readers because the evaluation protocol and the reporting of its limits can be transferred to other justice systems through retraining and local validation.

The manuscript "A Reproducible Methodological Framework for Prosecutorial Congestion Risk Prediction Using Explainable Machine Learning and Temporal Validation" has not been published elsewhere, is not under consideration by another journal, and reflects original research conducted by its authors. None of the authors have any conflicts of interest to disclose concerning this study.

Thank you for your valuable time.

Sincerely,

Moisés Evangelista Gamarra\
mevangelistag@senati.pe
